title: Role model & scoping spec for RBAC v2: hierarchical resources, scopes, and permissions matrix
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Objective: produce a definitive role model and permissions matrix for RBAC v2 that supports a hierarchical resource model (Organization -> Workspace -> Project -> Model -> Deployment/Endpoint) and explicit scopes (global, org, workspace, project, model, deployment). The design must integrate with SSO/SAML group assertions, support audit logging requirements, and provide admin controls (break-glass, emergency role elevation, role delegation).

Goals:
- Establish a minimal set of role primitives (Owner, Org Admin, Workspace Admin, Operator, Viewer, Billing, Security Auditor) that can be composed into custom roles.
- Define permission primitives (read, list, create, update, delete, invoke/generate, scale, rollback, manage-roles, manage-billing, view-audit-log) and map them to resource types.
- Define inheritance & evaluation rules across the hierarchy (explicit deny, explicit allow, inherited allow, least-privilege default).
- Define scoping model: role bindings may be attached at global (platform account), org, workspace, project, model, or deployment level. Higher-level bindings cascade unless an explicit override/deny exists at a lower level.
- Ensure SSO/SAML & SCIM workflows: group -> role binding sync, JIT provisioning, assertion mapping, fallback to email-based invite.
- Audit logging: required events, required fields (actor, actor_identity_source, action, resource_id, resource_type, scope, before/after where applicable), redaction rules for sensitive fields, retention classes.
- Admin controls: emergency access (timeboxed), session recording for admin actions, multi-person approval for high-risk ops, role delegation with expiration.

Resource hierarchy (canonical):
- organization (org) — top-level tenant.
- workspace — logical grouping for teams; workspace belongs to org.
- project — product-level grouping inside a workspace.
- model — served model artifact, can exist in multiple projects.
- deployment / endpoint — live inference endpoint tied to a model and infra.

Permission primitives (examples):
- read: view metadata/config (models, deployments).
- list: enumerate resources.
- create: create resource.
- update: modify resource config.
- delete: remove resource.
- invoke/generate: call the model/endpoint to generate tokens.
- manage-roles: create/edit bindings and role definitions.
- manage-billing: view/invoice/change billing settings.
- view-audit-log: access audit logs and export.
- escalate: perform emergency elevation operations (break-glass).

Roles (suggested default set):
- Platform Owner (global): full permission across orgs for super-admin tasks (reserved for SRE/Org Owner).
- Org Admin: manage org-level settings, users, billing, default role bindings.
- Workspace Admin: manage workspace resources and role bindings scoped to workspace.
- Operator: deploy/scale/rollback deployments; view metrics and logs for assigned scopes.
- Viewer: read/list only within scope.
- Billing: view and manage billing settings and invoices.
- Security Auditor: read audit logs, export, and run compliance queries; no write access.
- CustomRole: arbitrary composition of permission primitives; attachable at any scope.

Permissions matrix (high-level mapping):
- organization: manage-org-config (create/update/delete org metadata), manage-users, manage-billing, view-audit-log
- workspace: create/update/delete projects, manage-workspace-roles, list/workspace-resources
- project: create/update/delete models, assign-model-roles, list/models
- model: read/model-config, update/model-config, delete/model-version, create/deploy -> deployment, list/versions
- deployment: invoke/generate, scale, rollback, update/deploy-config, view-deployment-metrics

Evaluation semantics and inheritance:
- Bindings are (principal, role, scope, conditions, expires_at). Conditions support IP restrictions, time windows, and SAML-assertion constraints.
- Evaluation order: explicit deny at resource > explicit allow at resource > explicit deny at parent scope > explicit allow at parent scope > global default deny.
- Inheritance: role bindings at org level apply to all child scopes unless overridden. Lower-scope explicit deny supersedes parent allow.
- Role-merge: when a principal has multiple bindings, permissions are unioned except where a deny is present.

SSO/SAML & provisioning:
- Support mapping SAML group attributes to role bindings (group -> role at org/workspace scope).
- SCIM to provision users & groups; group-to-role bindings can be pushed via SCIM extension or mapped at the platform.
- JIT provisioning on first SAML login: create user account, attach groups from assertion. Provide audit event for created-by-sso and source-assertion.
- Conflict handling: on sync failure, create incident (audit event) and queue for manual reconciliation.

Audit logging requirements:
- Events to log: authentication, role binding CRUD, role definition CRUD, permission evaluation failures (denied access), resource CRUD, deployment lifecycle events (deploy/scale/rollback), billing changes, admin emergency elevation actions, SCIM syncs, SAML logins (with assertion id).
- Minimum fields: timestamp, event_id, actor_id, actor_identity_source (saml|scim|local), actor_ip, action, resource_type, resource_id, scope, outcome (success|denied|error), request_id, correlation_id, before_snapshot, after_snapshot (where applicable).
- Redaction: do not store raw prompt/user content for invoke events. Store only invocation metadata (length, tokens, model_id, request_id) unless customer opts-in.
- Retention classes: 90 days (default), 1 year (audit-sensitive), 7 years (regulatory hold). Provide export hooks for long-term archival.

Admin controls & security operations: 
- Break-glass: timeboxed escalation for Owner-level tasks. Requires justification, 2FA confirmation, and is recorded as high-sensitivity audit event.
- Emergency sessions: ephemeral tokens with strong TTL and admin session recording; must be approved by at least one other Org Admin for TTL > 30 mins.
- Role delegation: allow admins to delegate a subset of their roles with an expiration and optional approval chain.
- MFA enforcement and SSO enforcement policies per org.

Implementation notes & constraints:
- Policy store: use an append-only role bindings DB with change history to enable replays and audits.
- Fast-path evaluation: precompute effective roles for common principals scoped to org/workspace to minimize per-request latency. Cache invalidation on binding change.
- Back-compat: support existing RBAC v1 binders by mapping v1 roles into v2 canonical roles for a transitional period.
- Deny-first semantics must be efficient; represent denies as separate indexed records for checks.

Acceptance criteria:
- Completed role & permission matrix doc reviewed by Security, Product, and DevExp.
- Prototype evaluator with unit tests covering inheritance, denial, and multi-binding union.
- SCIM sync end-to-end test + SAML assertion mapping test.
- Audit events for role changes emitted to log pipeline with correct schema.

Links & artifacts:
- Design whiteboard: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/Sec/RBAC+v2+role+model
- Prototype PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/platform/pull/6132
- Audit schema proto: https://github.com/redwood-inference/observability/blob/main/protos/audit.proto

Open questions / trade-offs:
- Should we allow deny rules to be applied via SAML group sync (risk: accidental broad denies)? Proposal: deny rules are only platform-managed and cannot be set via SCIM.
- Granularity for model invocation metrics retention vs. privacy. Default to metadata-only retention unless explicitly enabled by customer.
- Whether to expose role composition UI in Console vs. only via API/CLI. Prioritize API-first with Console MVP for Org Admins.

Next steps:
1) Review with Security and Product on 2026-02-18 (done).
2) Finalize permission matrix and publish docs (owner: Marco).
3) Begin implementation of policy store + evaluator (owner: ENG-RBAC squad).
